Subject: SynthCraft x Redwood - SDK integration request

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for the quick intro last week — SynthCraft Labs is excited about a tighter integration with Redwood to surface our prompt-management and embedding SDKs inside partner apps. High level asks:

- A sandbox runtime where we can validate the LangChain/LlamaIndex connector pattern and verify tracing headers come through (we use X-Synth-Trace / OpenTelemetry spans).
- Token-level attribution metadata (for billing/QA) exposed in responses or logs if possible.
- A short joint evaluation (2-week PoC) focused on 1) realtime embeddings performance (cold/warm cache), 2) prompt-template round trips with function/tool calling, and 3) end-to-end trace visibility.

Attached is a one-pager with our desired integration checklist and sample client flow. Can your team share a tentative timeline and a sandbox credential? We have Ben (cc) who owns the SDK product — he can join the tech call.

Best,
Jane Park

Jane — great to meet you (virtually) and thanks for the doc. I'm copying Marissa (partnerships) and Karthik (serving/runtime) to scope the PoC and surface any constraints up front. Quick answers up front:

- Sandbox: we can provision a dedicated sandbox org on our staging cluster (token-based service account + short-lived keys).
- Tracing: Redwood supports OpenTelemetry and custom headers; Karthik, can we confirm X-Synth-Trace pass-through + trace-id correlation into our tracing backends?
- Attribution: we currently emit per-request metadata to logs and the console UI; token-level attribution to external systems is something we can surface via a telemetry export (we may need to scope sampling).

Proposed mutual action plan (draft):
1) Tech sync (30–45m) week of 4/26 to align on headers, expected payloads, and sample prompts.
2) Sandbox creds provisioned by 4/28.
3) Two-week PoC: 4/29–5/13 with weekly check-ins and a short results doc.
4) If PoC results hit stability / perf targets, draft MEP SOW and commercial terms.

I've attached a draft MEP SOW template to speed things up. Marissa — can you coordinate contract baseline and timelines with Jane? Karthik — any immediate red flags?

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz

Vanessa / Marissa — quick technical notes for the tech sync so we're aligned:

- Tracing: Redwood's ingress accepts custom trace headers and maps them to OpenTelemetry traces upstream. We generally honor incoming trace-ids if header present (we add our internal span ids). Please confirm SynthCraft will send a stable trace-id (X-Synth-Trace or traceparent). We can also emit a correlation id in responses (X-Redwood-Corr) to help partner debug.
- LangChain/LlamaIndex connector: recommend validating against our streaming and function-calling paths — prompt templates with tool calls tend to exercise async event loops and KV-cache hot paths.
- Token attribution: we can expose token-level logs to a partner-managed S3/GCS export, but not yet as a token-tag in the live response body for privacy/compat reasons. If they need token attribution in-app we can discuss an SDK wrapper that exchanges an attribution token and persists metadata in telemetry.
- Runtime constraints: for fair comparison we should capture sequence length distribution and batch sizes; ask them to provide representative workloads (5–10 sample prompts + expected average tokens per turn).

I'll join the 4/26 tech sync. If they want to instrument the LangChain connector, we can provide a small example repo showing trace propagation and a LlamaIndex index wrapper.

—Karthik
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
